An app without adds that provides full functionality and not only that, ACTUALLY WORKS. I will be donating, and I strongly encourage any users who can afford to, to donate also. Keep this gem free! Being able to set not only a custom delay but also a cooldown is a huge game changer from Apple screentime. With a 20s pause and 5 minute cooldown, after my session is over my brain has time to refocus instead of getting pulled right back in after a brief wait.  After a week, I’ve stuck to my 2 hr time limit and almost entirely stoped checking my problem apps. When I do, it’s much more intentional and I don’t get sucked in. I no longer feel the need to take my phone to the bathroom with me, or look at it as a social crutch or to pass time. I feel more present and am content to just watch the world go by. I am more focused and less forgetful.  I haven’t explored the full range of features because tbh, I haven’t needed them. The “intervention” tactic didn’t work for me bc it still kept me doing things on my phone, and my intent was to be OFF my phone. But I imagine it would be great if your goal is not total screentime reduction and just avoiding addictive apps.

TLDR: Brick is simple in both function and form. It's done what other blocking apps haven't, and makes my phone a tool and not a mind-numbing time-sucking addiction. It's also a one-time purchase and not yet another subscription. I consider the price of the Brick device a clever way these guys devised to get people to pay what a quality app and on going maintenance is worth. ——— I’ve tried Screentime, Freedom, and AppBlock. Screentime is a joke. Freedom and AppBlock each have pros and cons, including glitches where they'd sometimes work and sometimes not. What Brick has that none of these have is simplicity and a physical device.  The design is dark, boring, and plain, *which is exactly what these apps should be*. My desire is to stay off my phone, not get sucked into a brightly colored app with a statistics tab that I manage to waste 25 minutes on and have so many blocking options that scheduling them can act like a minor hobby. The statistics tab just shows you how long your phone was Bricked vs not Bricked. The scheduling options are either a blocklist or an allowlist and the day(s) and time(s) you want it active.  There's only one mode and the only way to turn it off is to tap my phone to a physical plastic square. This works *so well*. In most situations, that's enough to keep me from unbricking. I just really don't want to get up and walk across the kitchen or down the stairs in order to scroll Reddit. If I delete the app in order to turn off a session, I need to set everything up again when I reinstall it. There are only five emergency unbricks and I don't want to use one because I just had to watch YouTube while brushing my teeth. It also has yet to glitch and give me access when I shouldn't or block me when I should have access.  The only downside I've seen is if I forget to unbrick before I leave the house to go somewhere. But then again, do I REALLY need to ask ChatGPT if this new product at Costco is any good, check my email when standing in line, or order something from Amazon *that instant*? (No.)  This is actually helping me reconfigure my relationship to my phone and I barely have to think about it. It just works quietly in the background.  (I also like that this supports a small business in my home state.)

I’m enjoying the app. I love that it dims distracting apps on my phone so I know I can’t access them. Couple things I’ve noted in my use:  • Not sure if there was a proper walkthrough of each restriction option when I got the free trial, but I found I stuck to “Conscious Break” because that’s the first one I tried and didn’t know how the others worked. A pop up walkthrough would definitely encourage me to use more features  • I wish I could personalize the timer on how long I have to wait to take a conscious break. So, it starts at 5-6 seconds, but I need that to be at least 15 in order for me to give up and go back to my task (for a truly conscious break). Worried it created a bad habit where I just set my phone down and wait for the longer countdowns and take an unconscious break because the 5-6 second unlock time was too easy to get through  • I’m really not sure if there’s anything you can do about this one 😆 but when using the intention unlock feature, I’ve just typed a random letter to unlock it. Sometimes I use it properly—that helps my ADHD brain stay focused for sure. But I definitely get around it too quickly for it to be a truly conscious break  • It’d be great if the notifications of “time to get back to focusing” didn’t happen 30 seconds before the app closes. I wish it’d be more like 2 minutes before so I can save a video for later or wind down from my feed. I get frustrated and always fear losing the post when it kicks me out way too quickly.  I only tried the free version of Opal, but that was a little too hard to get into apps, and I think I rebelled a bit by the end and didn’t want to restrict myself at all. I like the flexibility of Jomo instead.    Overall, I’m not sure if I like this app or Opal Better. I think price is much better here. If you guys gamify Jomo the way Opal does (theirs is a bit overkill though) and tighten up some features, you’d have an incredible product.  All that being said, it’s definitely helped me focus. Keep up the good work.

I’m really liking this app so far and it’s teaching me just how bad my phone addiction is. I love that it lets you set limits on websites you visit too. This app is really helping me get back into hobbies I actually enjoy.   My one issue that I hope they can fix is that even though I have restricted an app to one minute (it’s a silly game that gets me hooked for hours) I can very easily go in and remove it from the list of what to limit even in strict mode. I know that there’s a level of responsibility on my part to not do that, but I would love it if I could set some kind of delayed response that would give me the time to contemplate if I really wanted to do that. For example, I would love it if I removed it from my list and instead of it happening right away it would remove it in 24 hours, in which I would be able to realize I don’t need it and cancel the removal.
